info.title: backend_si API
info.description:
JSON API consumed by the frontend.

This contract describes the behavior of every route (successes and errors).

**Session.** The session lives on the server and is identified by the `__Host-session` cookie (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/`, no `Max-Age`). Only `GET /api/csrf` creates a session: it starts an anonymous one when there is none. A successful login replaces it with a new session (new cookie and new CSRF token), and logout deletes it. A session ends after `SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT` without requests (default 15 minutes) or `SESSION_ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT` after login (default 8 hours), whichever comes first; the next request is then anonymous.

**CSRF.** Every state-changing request (any method other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS) must send the session cookie and the token returned by `GET /api/csrf` in the `X-CSRF-Token` header. The token changes at login: call `GET /api/csrf` again after logging in. Browser requests are also checked with Fetch Metadata: `Sec-Fetch-Site` must be `same-origin` or `none`, and without it an `Origin` that does not match the host is rejected. Clients that send neither header (curl, Bruno) only need the token.

**Access policy.** Each operation declares the `x-policy` extension: `"public"`, or the list of roles allowed to call it (`admin`, `comum`). Anonymous callers of a restricted operation get 401; authenticated callers without an allowed role get 403. The role is read from the database on every request, so a role change applies to the caller's next request, with no new login.

**Errors.** Every error response has the `ErrorResponse` body. `request_id` matches the `X-Request-Id` response header.

get.description: Reports that the process is serving HTTPS. It does not query the database.

Returns the CSRF token of the current session (anonymous or authenticated) and the header that must carry it. Starts an anonymous session when there is none; this is the only route that creates sessions. Call it again after login, because the token changes.

Set-Cookie.description: Only when the request had no valid session: the cookie of the new anonymous session (`__Host-session=<token>; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`).

post.description: Checks the credentials and starts a new authenticated session. Unknown users and wrong passwords get the same 401 response.

200.description: Logged in. A new session cookie is set.

Set-Cookie.description: The cookie of the new authenticated session, which replaces the anonymous one. The CSRF token changes too: call `GET /api/csrf` again.

post.description: Deletes the current session. The request has no body.

204.description: Logged out. The session no longer exists.

Set-Cookie.description: Expires the session cookie (`__Host-session=; Path=/; Max-Age=0; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`).

get.description: Returns who is authenticated, with which role, and the user's login and registration date.

post.description:
Creates a user with the given role. Only administrators can register users.

**400** (`bad_request`): the body is not well-formed for this operation: malformed JSON, a `Content-Type` other than `application/json`, an unknown field, or a field of the wrong JSON type (such as `"papel": 1`).

**422** (`unprocessable_entity`): the body is well-formed but a value is invalid: `login` does not match the login pattern (after lowercasing), `senha` has fewer than 15 or more than 128 characters, `papel` is not exactly `admin` or `comum`, or a field is missing.

**409** (`conflict`): the login is already taken, including by a login that differs only in case.

The response carries the normalized (lowercase) login.

get.description: Area restricted to the `comum` role. Administrators do not have access.

post.description:
Creates a support ticket for the `comum` user of the session. Administrators get 403.

`tipo` picks the type and `dados` carries only the fields of that type (see `CreateTicketRequest`). Text fields are trimmed and their lengths are counted in Unicode characters (code points). Single-line fields accept no control character, line break or tab; multi-line fields accept line feed, carriage return and tab only. `repositorio` must be an absolute `https://` URL with a host and no user name or password.

The author is the user of the session, the status is always `aberto`, and the id and the dates are set by the server: the body cannot carry them. Titles of `acesso`, `bug` and `deploy` tickets are built by the server: `Acesso a <sistema>`, `Bug em <sistema>`, `Deploy de <projeto> em <ambiente>` (with the environment label), cut to 120 characters; `outro` keeps `titulo`.

**400** (`bad_request`): the body is not well-formed for this operation: malformed JSON, a body that is not valid UTF-8, a `Content-Type` other than `application/json`, a key that is not one of the documented names spelled exactly (case-sensitive), a key of another type, a duplicate key (also when only the case differs), a field of the wrong JSON type, or `dados` missing or `null`. Keys the server owns (`author`, `user_id`, `status`, `id`, `created_at`, ...) are unknown keys.

**422** (`unprocessable_entity`): the body is well-formed but a value is invalid: an unknown `tipo`, a missing or empty required field, a length out of its limits, a forbidden character, a code outside its list, or a repository that is not an https URL. The answer never names the field.

**429** (`too_many_requests`): the user already sent 10 creation requests in the last 60 seconds. Every request that passes the CSRF check and the role check counts, valid or not; refused CSRF, anonymous and admin requests do not. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. The counts live in the memory of the backend process.

Nothing is stored when the answer is not 201. The response does not echo the field contents.

dados.justificativa: Preciso ver os painéis de monitoramento da equipe.

get.description:
"Meus tickets": the tickets whose author is the `comum` user of the session, and only those, whatever the query says. Administrators get 403 (they use `GET /api/administradores/tickets`).

Ordered by `updated_at`, most recent first, ties by `id`, highest first: a ticket with a new message or a new status moves to the top. Pages of 20 (`page_size`, fixed by the server). `total` counts every ticket that matches the filters; a page past the end answers 200 with no items and the real `total` and `pages`. An empty list is page 1 of 1.

Items never carry the fields of the type nor any author data.

**400** (`bad_request`): a parameter that is not `status`, `tipo` or `pagina` (`usuario` included: the author is always the session user), a parameter given twice, an empty value, a value outside its rule, or a malformed query string (a bad percent escape, a `;`). Nothing the client sends is silently ignored.

200.description: A page of the user's tickets.

get.description:
The ticket page of the `comum` user who wrote it: the summary plus every field of its type in `data`, under the same keys as `dados` of the creation request, stored as sent (trimmed). An empty optional field is `null`. The answer carries no author data. Administrators get 403 (they use `GET /api/administradores/tickets/{id}`).

**404** (`not_found`): the ticket does not exist, the id is not a positive integer written with digits only, or the ticket belongs to another user. The three cases get the same answer (status, headers and body); the attempt is logged with the user id and the ticket id.

200.description: The ticket with every field of its type.

get.summary: Read the thread of one of my tickets
get.description:
The conversation of a ticket of the `comum` user of the session: its messages and status changes, oldest first. Each entry says its `side` (`author`: the ticket's author; `support`: any administrator) and whether it is the caller's own (`mine`); it never carries an administrator's login or id. The opening of the ticket is not an entry (it is the ticket's `created_at`).

Pages of at most 100 entries: without `antes`, the latest ones; `has_more` is true when older entries exist, read with `antes` = the `id` of the first entry already shown.

**400** (`bad_request`): a parameter other than `antes`, `antes` given twice, empty, or not a positive integer, or a malformed query string.

**404** (`not_found`): as in `GET /api/tickets/{id}`, checked before the query.

200.description: A page of the thread, oldest first.

entries.text: O erro voltou hoje de manhã.

post.summary: Reply on one of my tickets
post.description:
Adds a message of the `comum` user of the session to the thread of their ticket. The text is plain text, stored trimmed; it is never interpreted as HTML or markdown. The author, the ticket and the date are set by the server: the body carries only `texto`. A reply never changes the status, but it moves the ticket's `updated_at` (and so its place in the lists).

**400** (`bad_request`): the body is not well-formed: not JSON, not valid UTF-8, `texto` missing, `null` or not a string, or any other key (`author`, `user_id`, `created_at`, `id`, `ticket_id`, `status`, ...), also a key spelled in another case or given twice.

**404** (`not_found`): as in `GET /api/tickets/{id}`.

**409** (`conflict`): the ticket is `fechado` and accepts no new message.

**422** (`unprocessable_entity`): the text, after trimming, is empty or longer than 2000 characters (Unicode code points), or holds a control character other than line feed, carriage return and tab.

**429** (`too_many_requests`): the user already sent 30 reply requests in the last 60 seconds. Every request that passes the CSRF and the role check counts, also one on someone else's ticket (answered 404); refused CSRF, anonymous and administrator requests do not. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. The counts live in the memory of the backend process and are shared with the administrators' replies of each user.

Nothing is stored when the answer is not 201.

example.texto:
O erro voltou hoje de manhã.
Segue o horário: 09:10.

201.description: The stored message, as it appears in the thread.

example.text:
O erro voltou hoje de manhã.
Segue o horário: 09:10.

get.description:
Every user's tickets, for administrators; `comum` users get 403 before any ticket is read. Same order, pages and page-past-the-end rule as `GET /api/tickets`. Items add the author's login. `status_counts` counts the tickets in each status over the whole queue, whatever the filters.

**400** (`bad_request`): a parameter that is not `status`, `tipo`, `usuario` or `pagina`, a parameter given twice, an empty value, a value outside its rule (`usuario` must follow the login rule), or a malformed query string.

200.description: A page of the queue and the status counts.

get.summary: List the authors of the queue
get.description:
The logins of the users who have at least one ticket, in byte order, at most 500: the options of the `usuario` filter of the queue. Administrators only.

**400** (`bad_request`): any query parameter (the operation reads none) or a malformed query string.

get.summary: Get a ticket of the queue
get.description:
Any user's ticket, for administrators: the answer of `GET /api/tickets/{id}` plus the author's login. `comum` users get 403, also for their own tickets, before any ticket is read.

**404** (`not_found`): the ticket does not exist or the id is malformed; both get the same answer.

200.description: The ticket with every field of its type and its author's login.

data.justificativa: Preciso ver os painéis da equipe.

get.summary: Read the thread of a ticket of the queue
get.description:
The thread of any ticket, for administrators: the answer of `GET /api/tickets/{id}/mensagens` where every entry adds `actor_login`, and `mine` is true for the caller's own entries only. Same pages, cursor and 400 rules.

**404** (`not_found`): the ticket does not exist or the id is malformed.

200.description: A page of the thread, oldest first.

entries.text: O erro voltou hoje de manhã.

post.summary: Reply on a ticket of the queue
post.description:
Adds a message of the calling administrator to any ticket's thread, with the rules of `POST /api/tickets/{id}/mensagens` (body, 400, 409, 422). Every administrator reply is visible to the author, who sees it on the `support` side with no login. It moves `updated_at` and never the status.

**404** (`not_found`): the ticket does not exist or the id is malformed.

**429** (`too_many_requests`): 30 reply requests in 60 seconds by the same administrator (their own quota, in the same limiter as the comum replies).

201.description: The stored message, as it appears in the admin thread.

TicketId.name: id
TicketId.description: Ticket number: digits only, no sign and no leading zero, from 1 to 9223372036854775807. Any other value is answered like a ticket that does not exist (404).

AntesQuery.name: antes
AntesQuery.description: Only entries older than the entry with this id (the first one already shown). Digits only, no sign and no leading zero. Absent: the latest entries.

UsuarioQuery.name: usuario
UsuarioQuery.description: Only tickets of the user with this login (the login rule: `^[a-z0-9._-]{3,64}$`). Absent: every user. Queue only.

StatusQuery.name: status
StatusQuery.description: Only tickets in this status. Absent: every status.

TipoQuery.name: tipo
TipoQuery.description: Only tickets of this type. Absent: every type.

PaginaQuery.name: pagina
PaginaQuery.description: Page number, from 1. Digits only, no sign and no leading zero. Absent: 1.

TicketClosed.description: The ticket is `fechado`: it accepts no new message.

example.message: Este ticket foi fechado e não aceita novas mensagens.

InvalidMessage.description: The text breaks the message rule. The answer never quotes it.

example.message: Dados inválidos. Revise os campos e tente novamente.

TicketNotFound.description: The ticket does not exist, the id is malformed, or (for a `comum` user) the ticket is someone else's. Every case gets the same answer.

BadQuery.description: A query parameter that the operation does not read, a parameter given twice, an empty value, a value outside its rule, or a malformed query string.

example.message: A requisição não pôde ser processada.

BadRequest.description: The body is not valid JSON, is empty, has unknown fields or data after the first JSON value, is larger than 64 KiB, or the `Content-Type` is not `application/json` (with no charset or `charset=utf-8`).

example.message: A requisição não pôde ser processada.

Unauthorized.description: Not authenticated (no session, or the session expired), or invalid credentials on login.

Forbidden.description: Missing or invalid CSRF token, a cross-origin browser request (Fetch Metadata), or a role that the operation does not allow.

example.message: Você não tem permissão para acessar este recurso.

Conflict.description: The login is already in use.

example.message: Este login já está em uso.
Dados inválidos. Revise os campos e tente novamente.

InvalidTicketData.description: A ticket value is invalid. The answer never says which field.

example.message: Dados inválidos. Revise os campos e tente novamente.

TooManyRequests.description: Too many requests by this user in a short time. Nothing was done.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the next request is accepted (1 to 60).

example.message: Muitas solicitações em pouco tempo. Aguarde um minuto e tente novamente.

InternalError.description: Unexpected error. Details go to the log, never to the client.

example.message: Ocorreu um erro inesperado. Tente novamente mais tarde.

created_at.description: When the user was registered (UTC). Sent by `GET /api/me` only.

header.description: Header that must carry the token.

error.description: Stable error code, such as `bad_request`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `conflict`, `unprocessable_entity`, `too_many_requests` or `internal`.

message.description: Generic message that is safe to show to the user.

request_id.description: Same value as the `X-Request-Id` header. Omitted in rare cases.

CreateTicketRequest.description: A ticket request: `tipo` and the `dados` of that type, with no other key.

repositorio.description: Absolute `https://` URL with a host and no user name or password. SSH addresses are refused.

observacoes.description: Optional. Multi-line. Absent, `null` and empty (after trimming) all mean no notes.

updated_at.description: Equal to `created_at` for a new ticket.

TicketSummary.description: A row of "Meus tickets". Never the fields of the type nor any author data.

updated_at.description: The last message or status change; `created_at` when there is none.

total.description: Tickets that match the filters, on every page.

pages.description: At least 1, also for an empty list.

AdminTicketSummary.description: A row of the queue: the summary plus the author's login. Never the author's id nor the fields of the type.

StatusCounts.description: Tickets in each status over the whole queue.

TicketDetail.description: A ticket with every field of its type. Never any author data.

data.description: The fields of `type`, under the keys of `dados` in the creation request; `null` for an empty optional field.

texto.description: Plain text, multi-line: 1 to 2000 characters after trimming; line feed, carriage return and tab are the only control characters allowed.

ThreadEntry.description: An entry of a ticket's thread as a `comum` user sees it: a message (`text`) or a status change (`from`, `to`). Never an administrator's login or id.

id.description: Entry id, in the order of the thread; the `antes` cursor.

mine.description: The entry was written by the caller.

text.description: The message as typed (trimmed). Plain text: never HTML or markdown.

has_more.description: Older entries exist: read them with `antes`.

AdminThreadEntry.description: `ThreadEntry` plus the login of who wrote it, for administrators.

mine.description: The entry was written by the calling administrator.

AdminTicketDetail.description: `TicketDetail` plus the author's login. Never the author's id.

DeployTicketDetailData.description: The fields of a `deploy` ticket as stored: `observacoes` is always present, `null` when it was left empty.

TicketStatus.description: A new ticket is always `aberto`; the other statuses belong to later features.
